content: The text provided is a list of references from various studies, reports, and articles related to HIV/AIDS, antiretroviral therapy (ART), and associated outcomes in different populations, particularly adolescents, children, and adults. 1. Provisional estimates of global disease burden can be accessed through the WHO's health information database, as of August 25, 2015. 2. The WHO report titled Health for the World’s Adolescents: A Second Chance in the Second Decade provides insights into adolescent health challenges and opportunities, accessed on August 25, 2015. 3. Auld AF et al. conducted a study comparing antiretroviral therapy (ART) enrollment characteristics and outcomes among HIV-infected adolescents, young adults, and older adults across seven African countries between 2004 and 2013. The findings were published in the MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2014. 4. Lamb MR et al. examined high attrition rates before and after ART initiation among youth aged 15–24 enrolled in HIV care. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2014. 5. Grimsrud A et al. analyzed outcomes of ART over a 10-year period of program expansion in African and Asian HIV programs. This multicohort analysis was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2014. 6. The Asia Pacific Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS published a report in 2013 titled Lost in Transitions, which highlights the challenges faced by adolescents living with HIV in the Asia-Pacific region. 7. Mavhu W et al. explored strategies to enhance psychosocial support for HIV-positive adolescents in Harare, Zimbabwe. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2013. 8. Denison J et al. investigated adherence to ART and HIV self-management from the perspectives of adolescents living with HIV and their caregivers. The study was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2015. 9. The WHO's guidance on HIV testing, counseling, and care for adolescents living with HIV provides recommendations for a public health approach, accessed on August 25, 2015. 10. Danel C et al. reported on the TEMPRANO trial, which evaluated early ART and isoniazid preventive therapy (IPT) in HIV-infected African adults with high CD4 counts. The trial findings were accessed on August 25, 2015. 11. Siegfried N et al. conducted a systematic review to determine the optimal timing for initiating ART in HIV-infected, treatment-naive children aged 2–5 years. The findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013. 12. Anglemeyer A et al. performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on universal ART for asymptomatic adults and adolescents with HIV-1 infection and CD4+ T-cell counts ≥500 cells/µL. The study remains unpublished. 13. The IeDEA Southern Africa, IeDEA West Africa, and COHERE collaborations conducted a causal modeling analysis to determine the appropriate timing for ART initiation in children and adolescents. The findings remain unpublished as of 2015. 14. Picat MQ et al. developed a cohort-based modeling study to predict long-term CD4 reconstitution patterns in HIV-infected children starting ART in sub-Saharan Africa. The study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2013. 15. Ferrand RA et al. investigated chronic lung disease in adolescents with delayed diagnosis of vertically acquired HIV infection. The study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2012. 16. Evans D et al. analyzed treatment outcomes of HIV-infected adolescents attending public-sector HIV clinics in South Africa. The findings were published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses in 2013. 17. Koech E et al. studied the epidemiology, social characteristics, and outcomes of HIV-infected youth and young adolescents enrolled in HIV care in Kenya. The study was published in AIDS in 2014. 18. Vinikoor MJ et al. demonstrated that age at ART initiation predicts immune recovery, mortality, and loss to follow-up among HIV-infected adults in urban Zambia. The study was published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses in 2014. 19. Berheto TM et al. identified predictors of loss to follow-up in patients living with HIV/AIDS after ART initiation. The study was published in the North American Journal of Medical Sciences in 2014. 20. Bygrave H et al. reported on ART outcomes among adolescents and youth in rural Zimbabwe. The study was published in PLoS One in 2012. 21. Nachega J et al. compared ART adherence, virologic, and immunologic outcomes in adolescents versus adults in southern Africa. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2009. 22. Kim SH et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on ART adherence in adolescents living with HIV. The study was published in AIDS in 2014. 23. Hudelson C and Cluver L reviewed factors associated with ART adherence among adolescents living with HIV/AIDS in lowand middle-income countries. The study was published in AIDS Care in 2015. 24. The PLATO II project team for the COHERE collaboration conducted a retrospective cohort study on the risk of triple-class virological failure in children with HIV. The study was published in The Lancet in 2011. 25. The Ministry of Health in Uganda documented the implementation of test-and-treat strategies for children and adolescents under 15 years of age in 2015. 26. A community-led consultation for the WHO 2015 consolidated treatment guidelines update assessed the acceptability of early ART initiation and viral load monitoring among service users and providers. 27. Ngokosin E et al. explored the treatment and care needs of adolescents living with HIV, emphasizing the importance of timely and consistent ART adherence. The findings remain unpublished as of 2014. 28. Mark D et al. conducted a situational analysis on the availability of appropriate HIV treatment and care services for adolescents in sub-Saharan Africa. 29. Bernays S et al. summarized findings from the ARROW and BREATHER qualitative research projects, addressing PICO questions for young people living with HIV in Uganda, Zimbabwe, the USA, the UK, and Ireland. 30. Koller M et al. examined immunodeficiency in children starting ART across low-, middle-, and high-income countries. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2015. 31. Barker PM and Mate K emphasized the need for significant improvements in maternal and child health services to eliminate mother-to-child HIV transmission. The study was published in Health Affairs in 2012. 32. The ARROW trial team compared routine versus clinically driven laboratory monitoring and first-line ART strategies in African children with HIV. The findings were published in The Lancet in 2013. 33. Baeten J et al. reported near elimination of HIV transmission in a demonstration project combining PrEP and ART. The findings were presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in 2015. 34. Grant RM et al. studied the uptake of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), sexual practices, and HIV incidence in men and transgender women who have sex with men. The study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2014. 35. Martin M et al. provided preliminary follow-up data on injecting drug users receiving PrEP. 36. Baeten JM et al. evaluated ART prophylaxis for HIV prevention in heterosexual men and women. The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2012.
